heroAnswer: Sidney was picked for the courthouse, built on the canal, and kept by the factories — and its houses are old enough to remember all three. We serve Sidney with free inspections, transparent pricing, and photo-documented work.
intro: Sidney is our service area's third county seat and northernmost town — laid out in 1819 on the west bank of the Great Miami, about 40 miles north of Dayton. Its story runs canal (1825–1837) to rail (1851/1856) to I-75 (four interchanges). Housing is an even-spread old stock: median build 1971, 62.4% pre-1980, 22.1% pre-1939. No Sidney tornado and no Sidney levee shield are claimed — the river town above the shield, where the check-the-address line carries the weight.
